title: Coproducts of flat module sheaves are flat
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site and $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$, and let $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ be the category of sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. If $(\mathcal M_b)_{b\in B}$ is a set-indexed family of flat sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], then the coproduct $\coprod_{b\in B}\mathcal M_b$ in $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ is flat over $\mathcal O$.

source.place: Lemma 18.28.5 (Tag 03EU), clause (2), direct sums of flat sheaves of modules are flat

proof.text: By the project size convention [def-weil-size-convention], replace the site by its chosen small skeleton. Then [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] gives that $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ is Grothendieck abelian. By [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed], its sheaf tensor product is symmetric monoidal closed. For each $b$, the exact functor $\mathcal G\mapsto\mathcal G\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal M_b$ in the definition [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] is transported by the symmetry isomorphism to $\mathcal M_b\otimes_{\mathcal O}-$, so it preserves finite limits; thus every $\mathcal M_b$ is flat in the sense of [lem-weil-pbc-flat-coproduct].

source.place: Lemma 03EU, clause (2), together with Definition 03ER, item (3), and Section 03EK

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-coproduct] to the Grothendieck abelian braided closed monoidal category $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ and the family $(\mathcal M_b)_{b\in B}$. It says that $\coprod_{b\in B}\mathcal M_b$ preserves finite limits after tensoring on the left. The symmetry again identifies this with exactness of $\mathcal G\mapsto\mathcal G\otimes_{\mathcal O}(\coprod_b\mathcal M_b)$, which is precisely flatness in [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules].
